Watch/Legends|Death Watch]] }} {{Quote|The Concordian moon is a province, with its own governor.|[[Duchess/Legends|Duchess]] [[Satine Kryze/Legends|Satine Kryze]]|}} '''Concordia''' was one of two [[Moon/Legends|moons]] [[Orbit/Legends|orbiting]] the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]]. A verdant moon possessing dense [[Tree/Legends|forests]], the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]] originally settled Concordia as an agricultural colony. However, during the [[Time/Legends|time]] of war, the Mandalorians established a vast number of [[Mining/Legends|mining]] camps on the moon in search of [[Beskar/Legends|''beskar'']] [[Iron/Legends|iron]], a nearly indestructible metal [[Ore/Legends|ore]] unique to Mandalore and its orbiting [[Satellite/Legends|satellite]]. The excessive strip-mining operation almost destroyed Concordia's forests, though by [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], they were making a recovery. [[Standard century/Legends|Centuries]] after the [[Mandalorian Excision|rise]] of the pacifistic [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorian]] faction, the violent renegade sect of Mandalorians known as the [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]] incited numerous Mandalorian clan [[Chief/Legends|leaders]] to war against their peaceful regime in a conflict that became known as the [[Great Clan Wars/Legends|Great Clan Wars]]. The Death Watch-backed [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]] were eventually defeated, reluctantly accepting [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exile]] to Concordia, an independent Mandalorian province the rule of which was turned over to [[Clan Vizsla/Legends|Clan Vizsla]]. By the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|beginning]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], Concordia was [[Governor/Legends|governed]] by [[Pre Vizsla/Legends|Pre Vizsla]], a public supporter of New Mandalorian [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|leader]] [[Duchess/Legends|Duchess]] [[Satine Kryze/Legends|Satine Kryze]], but secretly the leader of a reborn faction of Death Watch. Vizsla established a [[Death Watch hideout|Death Watch base]] in the moon's [[Concordian mines/Legends|abandoned mines]], where he worked in secret to rebuild the Death Watch. His base was [[Fight on Concordia/Legends|discovered]] by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] during an investigation of the Death Watch's presence in current Mandalorian affairs, and his efforts to turn the New Mandalorians against the Republic were [[Mandalore Defense Resolution/Legends|thwarted]] by the combined actions of Kenobi and Duchess Kryze. With Vizsla's ties to Death Watch were exposed to all, he lost his position as governor of Concordia, and was eventually forced to abandon the Mandalorian moon to join Death Watch in a nomadic existence wandering [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], until he led a [[Takeover of Mandalore/Legends|coup]] against the New Mandalorians to take power. ==Description== {{Quote|I thought Concordia was an agricultural settlement.''"
"''Before the end of our wars, they turned it into a mining base. The sheer number of mining facilities here nearly destroyed our forests. They're finally growing back.|[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and Satine Kryze|}} Concordia was a terrestrial [[Moon/Legends|moon]], one of two [[Satellite/Legends|satellites]] that [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]], the cultural [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] people, located in the [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalore sector]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. One of several habitable locations in the [[Mandalore system/Legends|Mandalore system]], Concordia was a lush, temperate moon, with chains of [[Mountain/Legends|mountains]] dotting its surface. As the [[Star system/Legends|system's]] [[Mandalore (star)/Legends|sun]] set, Concordia could be seen from the surface of Mandalore as a [[Color/Legends|green]] sphere in the evening sky. [[File:ConcordianLandscape.png|thumb|left|300px|Concordia's rural landscape]] A verdant moon where dense forests grew, Concordia became an [[Agriworld/Legends|agricultural colony]] after being settled by the Mandalorians. The Mandalorian moon was home to a number of animals, including [[Diet/Legends|carnivorous]] predators who were known to chance attacking [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] prey at night. Individuals who ventured out into the Concordian plains in the dark could ward off the moon's predators with fire.{{TORweb|url=info/news/blog/20141028|text="Bedtime on Concordia"|int=Bedtime on Concordia}} During the period when Mandalore continued to engage in large-scale warfare, Concordia became the target of [[Beskar/Legends|''beskar'']] [[Iron/Legends|iron]] [[Mining/Legends|miners]], who scoured the moon for the nearly indestructible metal.{{InsiderCite|80|The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors}} Unsightly mines marred much of Concordia's surface, almost destroying the moon's forests in the process. Even after the Mandalorians' wars came to an end, it was only around the time of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] that the Concordian forests began to make a recovery. The old mines were abandoned to fall into disrepair, a symbol of the mining industry left behind, only be revitalized by the radical [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]] splinter sect to serve as [[Death Watch hideout|hidden bases]] for their operations on Concordia and a place to manufacture [[Armor/Legends|armor]] and munitions in secret. ==History== {{Quote|Some unrepentant mercenaries and warriors were exiled to the moon Concordia, while others dispersed throughout the galaxy, resuming the Mandalorians' ancient trade as blasters-for-hire.|[[Vilnau Teupt]]|''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''}} [[File:ConcordianMines-Overview.png|thumb|right|300px|[[Beskar/Legends|''Beskar'']] iron [[Concordian mines/Legends|mines]] marred Concordia's lush surface]] The early Mandalorian [[Taung/Legends|Taung]] conquered the uninhabited world that would become Mandalore around [[7000 BBY]], naming the world for their leader, [[Mandalore the First/Legends|Mandalore the First]]. As they set out to capture the surrounding worlds of the Mandalore system, the Mandalorians eventually turned their sights on the lush and forested moon of Concordia. Over time, the verdant moon became an agricultural settlement, inhabited and tended by Mandalorian [[Farmer/Legends|farmers]]. During the [[Galactic War]], the Mandalorian [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] [[Galron (Mandalorian)|Galron]] made camp on Concordia with his [[twin]] daughters [[Mari (Mandalorian)|Mari]] and [[Tayn]]. Around the [[Fire/Legends|fire]], they spoke of the famed warrior [[Mandalore the Avenger|Shae Vizla]] and the ancient [[Mandalore the Conqueror]], before the [[Gender/Legends|girls]] drifted off to [[Sleep/Legends|sleep]] under their [[Parent/Legends|father's]] watchful [[Eye/Legends|eye]]. Eventually, interest in Concordia turned away from agriculture and in the direction of mining. As the Mandalorians continued to wage war [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] prior to [[Declaration of a New Order|rise]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], they sought ''beskar'' iron ore from beneath the surface of Concordia. The metal was a [[Galaxy/Legends|galactic]] rarity, found only on Mandalore''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]'' and its moon, and was prized for its nigh invulnerability, capable of withstanding the blows of a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]]. Ugly mines came to scar the surface of Concordia, and the Mandalorians' strip-mining efforts were so extensive that the moon's native forests were nearly destroyed. Following the [[Mandalorian Excision]]—a brief but overwhelming conflict between the Mandalorians and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] that transformed portions of Mandalore into barren [[Desert/Legends|deserts]] of [[white]] sand—a reformist [[Politics/Legends|political]] faction of Mandalorians was born: the [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorians]]. The New Mandalorians believed in pacifism, and sought to establish a peaceful society isolated from the traditional warrior clans. Rogue elements within the warrior clans worked to see the New Mandalorians' downfall for centuries, eventually culminating with the foundation of the [[Death/Legends|Death]] Watch splinter group under [[Tor Vizsla]] around [[60 BBY/Legends|60 BBY]]. In an attempt to see the New Mandalorians' downfall, Death Watch incited a number of clan [[Chief/Legends|chieftains]] to war against the pacifists, though other clan leaders rose to defend them. In the end, the [[Great Clan Wars/Legends|Great Clan Wars]] resulted in a defeat for Death Watch, and the beaten but unrepentant clan [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]] accepted [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exile]] to Concordia. Control of the Mandalorian moon was turned over to [[Clan Vizsla/Legends|Clan Vizsla]], to act as a province independent of the New Mandalorian state. [[File:VizslaVilla-TMP.png|thumb|left|300px|A Mandalorian [[Unidentified Concordia city/Legends|settlement]] on Concordia]] By the start of the [[Cloning/Legends|Clone]] Wars in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], more than a [[Standard decade/Legends|decade]] after the end of the Great Clan Wars, it was the position of the New Mandalorian [[Ruling Council (New Mandalorians)/Legends|government]] that the warriors that had been exiled to Concordia had died since out. During this time, Concordia was ruled by Governor [[Pre Vizsla/Legends|Pre Vizsla]], an outward supporter of the New Mandalorians and friend to their leader, [[Duchess/Legends|Duchess]] [[Satine Kryze/Legends|Satine Kryze]]. In secret, however, Vizsla was the [[Secret Mandalore|leader]] of the Death Watch, rebuilding the sect in the wake of the Great Clan Wars. Vizsla established a base of operations in the abandoned ''beskar'' mines of Concordia, using the facilities to manufacture [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|Mandalorian armor]] and armament, and as a staging ground for his Death Watch forces. Vizsla's plans and the Death Watch's secret base were uncovered by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and Duchess Kryze during a visit to Concordia in the early [[Standard month/Legends|months]] of the Clone Wars. Discovered, Vizsla [[Fight on Concordia/Legends|fought]] Kenobi to a draw, and a trio of his Death Watch [[Troop/Legends|troops]] forced the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] Master to retreat with the Duchess back to Mandalore. Even still, Vizsla continued to use Concordia and his base there as a staging ground for a planned Death Watch takeover of Mandalore. There, he amassed an [[Army/Legends|army]] of soldiers, but before an attack could be made, [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]]—Vizsla's ally in the Confederacy of Independent Systems—ordered his men to stand down due to the veto of a Republic [[Mandalore Defense Resolution/Legends|defense initiative]] that would have sent a [[Garrison/Legends|contingent]] of [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] to Mandalore. Vizsla and Dooku had planned to use the Republic occupation to sway the Mandalorian populace to support Death Watch as would-be liberators against an oppressive offworld force. Without the backing of Mandalore's people, Death Watch did not have the strength to take control of the planet.{{TCW|Duchess of Mandalore}} Death Watch was later driven from Concordia and the surrounding [[Mandalore system/Legends|Mandalore system]], eventually establishing a [[Carlac Death Watch camp/Legends|camp]] on the far away world of [[Carlac/Legends|Carlac]].{{TCW|A Friend in Need}} By the Clone Wars' end, Concordia had acquired a reputation for doing business with a number of [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] and [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] that operated in and around Mandalorian [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. Areas of the moon were known to host an ostensible presence of the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] crime syndicate, operating under the oversight of [[Vigo/Legends|Vigo]] [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor's]] [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]], [[Tyno Fabris]]. Non-Mandalorian offworlders with business on the Mandalorian homeworld would occasionally make planetfall on Concordia to fulfill their needs, rather than journeying down to the surface of Mandalore itself.[[The Last Jedi (novel)|''The Last Jedi'']] ==Inhabitants== {{Quote|You won't make much progress without me there, especially since you've just been involved with the death of a Concordian.|Satine Kryze|}} [[File:Vizsla_welcomes_Satine.png|thumb|right|300px|Concordian Governor [[Pre Vizsla/Legends|Pre Vizsla]] and his [[Mandalorian Guard/Legends|armored guards]]]] Concordia was first inhabited by members of the Mandalorian culture as an agricultural settlement, becoming a home to a number of Mandalorian farmers. Later, the moon was transformed into a mining base, and Concordia became a haven for ''beskar'' miners, operating the numerous mines littered across the moon's surface. The people of Concordia were collectively known as Concordians, and spoke a dialect of [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']]—the traditional Mandalorian [[Language/Legends|language]]''[[Republic Commando: Order 66]]''—also known as [[Concordian]], a dialect shared by the nearby world of [[Concord Dawn/Legends|Concord Dawn]]. In the aftermath of the Great Clan Wars, several unrepentant warrior clan chieftains who had sided with Death Watch to dethrone the New Mandalorians went into exile on Concordia upon their defeat. The rule of the Mandalorian moon was entrusted to the members of Clan Vizsla, and by the time of the Clone Wars, Concordia was recognized as an independent province, separate from the New Mandalorian state and ruled by its own governor. ==Behind the scenes== The moon of Concordia was first introduced to the ''[[Star Wars]]'' universe in the twelfth episode of the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' television series']] [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|second season]], entitled "[[The Mandalore Plot]]." The Mandalorian moon made subsequent appearances in the following episodes "[[Voyage of Temptation]]"{{TCW|Voyage of Temptation}} and "[[Duchess of Mandalore]]," before receiving a mention in the [[The Clone Wars: Season Five|fifth season]] episode "[[Shades of Reason]]."{{TCW|Shades of Reason}} The novels ''[[The Clone Wars: Darth Maul: Shadow Conspiracy]]'' and [[The Last Jedi (novel)|''The Last Jedi'']] made additional mentions of Concordia, as did the young reader book ''[[The Clone Wars: Secret Missions 4: Guardians of the Chiss Key]]'',''[[The Clone Wars: Secret Missions 4: Guardians of the Chiss Key]]'' and the [[Star Wars: The Old Republic|''The Old Republic'']] web short "[[Bedtime on Concordia]]." Although ''[[The Essential Atlas]]''—a galactic geography reference book [[Author/Legends|authored]] by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Daniel Wallace]], and published [[August 18]], [[2009]]—was the first source to state Mandalore was orbited by two moons, Concordia was the first to be introduced by name. Fry's later sourcebooks ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: New Battlefronts: The Visual Guide]]'' and ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Incredible Vehicles]]'' featured additional information on the Concordian moon,''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Incredible Vehicles]]'' and ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' Fry co-wrote with [[Paul R. Urquhart]] gave further mention and information of Concordia. ==Appearances== *{{TORweb|url=info/news/blog/20141028|text="Bedtime on Concordia"|int=Bedtime on Concordia}} *''[[The Clone Wars: Secret Missions 4: Guardians of the Chiss Key]]'' {{Mo}} *{{TCW|The Mandalore Plot}} {{1st}} *{{TCW|Voyage of Temptation}} {{Flash}} *{{TCW|Duchess of Mandalore}} *''[[The Clone Wars: Darth Maul: Shadow Conspiracy]]'' {{Mo}} *{{TCW|Shades of Reason}} {{Mo}} *[[The Last Jedi (novel)|''The Last Jedi'']] {{Mo}} ==Sources== {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of Concordia}} *{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode212.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: The Mandalore Plot}} {{1stm}} *[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Comic 6.6|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Comic 6.6]] *''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: New Battlefronts: The Visual Guide]]'' *[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Two|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season Two]] *''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Incredible Vehicles]]'' *''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' *''[[Star Wars: The Ultimate Visual Guide: Updated and Expanded]]'' *''[[Star Wars: The Bounty Hunter Code]]'' *{{SWE|groups|deathwatch|Death Watch}} *{{SWE|technology|gauntlet-fighter|Gauntlet fighter}} ==Notes and references== {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |de=Concordia#legends |es=Concordia/Leyendas |fr=Concordia |nl=Concordia |pl=Concordia/Legendy }} [[Category:Agriworlds]] [[Category:Arboreal moons]] [[Category:Mandalore system locations]] [[Category:Mining moons]] [[Category:Moons in the Outer Rim Territories]] [[Category:Moons in the Trans-Hydian Borderlands]] {{RelatedCategories |[[Category:Concordia locations]] }}
